svg.text: Detailed current-state architecture derived from the present repository structure, runtime flows, and deployment assets in the CropSentinel codebase.

g.text: System Summary

Two React portals share one frontend codebase: a tenant customer portal and a separate platform-admin portal. Both talk to a FastAPI backend that exposes REST APIs and a shared admin WebSocket. Endpoint agents run on monitored machines, stream activity over WebSocket first with HTTP fallback, store unsent work locally, and participate in live-view / remote-access WebRTC sessions through backend signaling.

Core storage is PostgreSQL with tenant-scoped tables, time-partitioned activity logs, JSON settings and policy documents, evidence objects, alert queues, DLP incidents, phishing incidents, and machine health. Redis is used when configured for multi-instance WebSocket fanout and online-machine coordination; otherwise the backend falls back to single-instance in-memory delivery.
1. User and Access Layer
HUMAN ACCESS
Customer Portal Users
Admin, manager, viewer, and remote_operator roles authenticated with tenant-scoped JWTs.
Main pages: Dashboard, Machines, Teams, Live View, Remote Access, App Usage, Browser Logs, Productivity, Input, Files, Network, DLP, Phishing, Alerts, Reports, Users, Settings.
Permissions mirror backend role checks such as machines.view, alerts.manage, remote.access, reports.generate, settings.edit.
Single shared admin WebSocket per browser session receives machine-online state, screenshots, alerts, DLP/phishing updates, and WebRTC signaling.
PLATFORM ACCESS
Platform Admin Portal
Separate login path and separate token storage for platform routes.
Main pages: Overview, Tenant Management, Platform Users, Platform DLP baseline, Platform Phishing baseline.
Platform tenant is enforced as tenant_id=1 for platform-admin guarded routes.
Creates and updates tenants, rotates enrollment tokens, packages installer bundles, and manages platform-wide baseline policy defaults.
FRONTEND APP
Shared React + Vite Frontend
`frontend/src/main.jsx` defines lazy-loaded route trees, `PrivateRoute` for customer pages, and `PlatformPrivateRoute` for platform pages.
`useAuth.jsx` provides REST fetch helpers, one session-wide `/ws/admin` connection, error normalization, token persistence, and API-base environment handling via `VITE_API_URL`.

Sentry browser SDK is optional via env. Notification and page-context providers wrap the route tree. The frontend ships as a separate container in `docker-compose.yml` and serves the portals over port 80.
Logical outcome: one UI codebase, two access contexts, one backend API surface, one shared realtime event channel per signed-in browser session.
2. API and Realtime Control Plane
FASTAPI BACKEND
Unified Backend Runtime
`backend/main.py` composes routers for auth, platform, users, machines, analytics, teams, alerts/settings, DLP enterprise, phishing, sessions, data logs, tenants, database admin, and WebSockets.
AUTHORIZATION + TENANT CONTEXT
JWT login for customer and platform portals.
Middleware decodes tenant_id, role, username, sets DB tenant context, and tags Sentry context.
Role permissions and machine scoping enforced before route access.
License feature checks gate remote access and other premium capabilities.
LIFECYCLE + DEFAULTS
Boot flow loads and verifies the license, seeds default settings, admin user, and baseline alert rules.
Background Redis subscriber task is started if `REDIS_URL` exists.
Seat enforcer and agent API-key expectations are attached to app state.
Operational knobs include screenshot cadence, baseline inventory defaults, and self-throttle defaults.
ROUTERS / DOMAIN SURFACES
Monitoring: machines, analytics, browser/app/file/network/input activity, screenshots, reports.
Security: alert rules/logs, audit logs, DLP policy/rules/incidents, phishing policy/incidents.
Admin: tenants, platform stats, platform users, DB admin, settings, sessions.
Both REST ingestion and WebSocket ingestion land in the same backend service layer and DB methods.
WEBSOCKET CONTROL PLANE
`/ws/admin`: browser sessions subscribe once per login, receive scoped tenant events, request screenshots, and initiate WebRTC session signaling.
`/ws/agent/{machine_id}`: authenticated agent sockets push browser/app/screenshot/file/network/input/DLP/phishing/heartbeat events and receive config or command acks.
Offline grace logic broadcasts `machine_unstable` then `machine_offline`, evaluates connectivity alerts, and terminates related WebRTC sessions if the agent stays absent.
Redis-backed broadcast and per-agent command channels are used only when `REDIS_URL` is configured; otherwise the same `ConnectionManager` runs in-memory.
SESSION + REMOTE ACCESS PATH
REST session endpoints return machine capabilities and handshake metadata for `live` or `remote` sessions.
`webrtc_manager.py` is a signaling relay only: the backend routes SDP/ICE between browser and agent but does not carry media.
Remote commands are validated against an allowlist: lock screen, show message, open URL, mute/unmute audio, sleep, logout user, ctrl-alt-del.
Live view can degrade to JPEG screenshot polling when full WebRTC streaming is not active.
SERVICE DOMAINS
Business Services and Workflows
ACTIVITY INGEST
Validates payload sizes, deduplicates event IDs, normalizes machine payloads, and routes inserts plus alert evaluation.
Used by both HTTP routes and WebSocket event handling.
Event types: browser, application, screenshot, heartbeat, input, file, network.
DLP ENTERPRISE
Versioned policies, rules, classifiers, exceptions, incident grouping, simulation, diagnostics, and baseline status APIs.
Legacy `/api/dlp/events` remains active for event ingestion compatibility.
High-risk events auto-create alert logs and broadcast tenant-scoped alert updates.
PHISHING DOMAIN
Tenant effective policies, platform baseline, event ingestion, grouped incidents, allowlists, whitelists, blacklists, and diagnostics.
Browser-driven warn-only protection is the current coverage model, with unsupported channels degrading visibly.
TENANT OPERATIONS
Tenant CRUD, seat and expiry metadata, enrollment-token rotation, and tenant-specific downloadable agent bundles.
Download bundle includes installer artifact plus generated `config.env` and README.
Windows bundle expects a prebuilt `cropsentinel-agent-*.exe` in `backend/dist/installers`.
3. Data Plane, Persistence, and Endpoint Runtime
PERSISTENT DATA
PostgreSQL Core Store
Tenant root tables: tenants, machines, teams, team_memberships, users, settings, tenant_config_documents, audit_logs, alert_rules, alert_logs.
Time-partitioned activity streams: browser_activity, app_activity, file_activity, network_activity, and related analytics-facing tables.
Security and evidence: screenshots, evidence_objects, DLP event / incident / policy / classifier / exception data, phishing events / incidents / lists, machine `agent_health` JSON snapshots.
Machine rows carry last_seen, active_app, idle_seconds, CPU, memory, agent_version, tenant binding, and structured health telemetry used by diagnostics and self-throttle visibility.
Settings are keyed per tenant. Policy-style documents are stored as JSON payloads so agents can receive effective config through heartbeat responses.
Reports are generated through backend routes and saved in the reports volume. License information and feature gating also live in the backend runtime and tenant metadata.
Compose uses PostgreSQL 16 as the system database and mounts a persistent named volume for data durability.
OPTIONAL BUS
Redis Coordination Layer
Channels:
`croppro:events` for cross-instance admin event fanout.
`croppro:agent:{machine_id}` for cross-instance commands to connected agents.
`croppro:online` set for global online machine tracking.
When `REDIS_URL` is absent, this entire layer is bypassed and the backend behaves as a single-instance node with local memory state only.
Compose includes Redis 7 by default, so the current intended deployment shape supports horizontal-safe event routing even though single-instance fallback exists.
ENDPOINT AGENT
Agent Runtime on Monitored Machines
`agent/agent.py` orchestrates machine identity, consent/config files, runtime intervals, local queueing, heartbeat exchange, realtime transport, and module startup.

Telemetry modules: browser history, screenshots, application activity, input activity, file tracking, network tracking, USB tracking, print tracking, phishing protection, WebRTC agent, baseline inventory.
Transport model: WebSocket-first to `/ws/agent/{machine_id}` with event acknowledgements, plus REST fallback endpoints for batch / activity uploads.
Local persistence includes an encrypted SQLite-backed offline queue for unsent events and a fingerprint/inventory SQLite store for baseline file scanning.

Self-throttle policy can stretch screenshot, heartbeat, browser, network, USB, print, and file-cache sweep intervals based on CPU, memory, and queue depth while still reporting effective runtime state back to the server.
Agent config is hot-reloaded from heartbeat responses, including DLP policy, phishing policy, baseline inventory settings, and performance controls.
Primary Runtime Flows
Portal REST + shared admin WebSocket traffic
Agent telemetry, heartbeat config, and WebRTC signaling
Persistence and packaging paths (DB, evidence, installer, baseline sync)

Repository signals represented here: `frontend/src/main.jsx`, `frontend/src/hooks/useAuth.jsx`, `backend/main.py`, `backend/app/core.py`, `backend/app/lifecycle.py`, `backend/app/ws_service.py`, `backend/app/db/schema.py`, `backend/app/routers/*.py`, `backend/webrtc_manager.py`, `agent/agent.py`, `agent/baseline_inventory.py`, `backend/redis_bus.py`, `docker-compose.yml`.
